newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA's Thompson warns banks about loan quality.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA's Thompson warns banks about loan quality.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) deputy governor Graeme Thompson said on Thursday that the lending policies of private sector banks could lead to credit quality problems with corporate and mortgage loans.

"On balance, we believe that some current lending practices do risk sowing seeds of future credit quality problems for banks," Thompson said in a speech to a business luncheon entitled "The Many Faces of Risk in Banking".

"Chief executives and boards should be considering carefully whether the additional point of market share that might be won now by lending to marginal propositions is worth the pain of future losses, the resources needed for loan workouts, and so on.

"They should also be alert to the possibility that the household sector might feature more strongly in the next upswing of losses. Household debt has increased a good deal more quickly than incomes in recent years."

Thompson said that in general, the private banks had a better handle on credit risk than they did 10 years ago or in the late 1980s and early 1990s when they wrote off A$25 billion in loan losses. He also said corporate structures which contributed to the previous problems had changed for the better.
"This is all reassuring, but it is certainly no reason for complacency," he said.
"There is little doubt that current lending standards are less stringent than they were a couple of years ago.
"Our observations during visits to banks support the market anecdotes on this," he said.

The warnings by Thompson follow a newspaper report earlier this week that RBA governor Ian Macfarlane had recently told foreign banks that the central bank was worried about a deterioration of the quality of corporate loans.
